title: Rotated two-stage GWAS with rotationGWAS
text: first stage mixed model plot data whose terms depend design trial. shipped panels paper’s model: line environment fixed effects, replicate within environment line--environment random effects. adjusted means estimated marginal means lines variance-covariance matrix Kenward-Roger adjusted one, emmeans. chunk repeats first stage dense panel checks shipped values; first-stage software yields means full variance-covariance matrix can take place.
code: plots <- panel_dense$plots head(plots, 3) #>   accession environment replicate     y #> 1      L001         E01         1 47.44 #> 2      L001         E02         1 39.40 #> 3      L001         E03         1 43.69 ## The first-stage model, fitted by REML. m1 <- lme4::lmer(y ~ accession + environment + (1 | environment:replicate) + (1 | accession:environment),                  data = plots, REML = TRUE) ## The adjusted means and their variance-covariance matrix. emm <- emmeans::emmeans(m1, ~ accession, mode = "kenward-roger") s1 <- summary(emm) means <- setNames(s1$emmean, as.character(s1$accession)) Omega <- as.matrix(vcov(emm)) dimnames(Omega) <- list(names(means), names(means)) all.equal(means, panel_dense$means) #> [1] TRUE all.equal(Omega, panel_dense$Omega) #> [1] TRUE

title: Rotated two-stage GWAS with rotationGWAS
text: print summarises Ω\Omega gives model without marker. plot shows structure Ω\Omega: dense panel means nearly uncorrelated, sparse panel lines share environments strongly correlated, environment effects estimated lines.
code: ## The rotation of the dense and of the sparse panel. rd <- rotation(panel_dense$means, panel_dense$Omega, A, Q) rs <- rotation(panel_sparse$means, panel_sparse$Omega, A, Q) rd #> Rotation of 150 adjusted means; 4 fixed effects (the rotated intercept and 3 covariates )   #> Omega: diagonal from 1.8 to 1.88 (ratio 1.04); mean |correlation| 0.0285, largest 0.0722; condition number 5.96 #> Model without a marker: genetic variance 14.42, residual variance 1.338 (target one) #> With the residual variance fixed at one: genetic variance 15.75 rs #> Rotation of 150 adjusted means; 4 fixed effects (the rotated intercept and 3 covariates )   #> Omega: diagonal from 7.14 to 22.6 (ratio 3.17); mean |correlation| 0.443, largest 0.915; condition number 517 #> Model without a marker: genetic variance 14.17, residual variance 1.325 (target one) #> With the residual variance fixed at one: genetic variance 15.78 ## The absolute correlations of the adjusted means, in the order of the lines. op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1)) plot(rd, main = "dense panel") plot(rs, main = "sparse panel") par(op)

what: The residual variance of the rotated model
title: Rotated two-stage GWAS with rotationGWAS
text: rotation estimation errors means unit variance, residual variance rotated model without marker one relationship matrix accounts genetic covariance among accessions. specification_test() tests one increase REML deviance fixed one: one-sided 2.71, test paper recommends, genetic structure missing model raises residual variance; two-sided 3.84. tests can read profile-likelihood intervals, plot shows profile deviance.  Neither dense sparse panel rejects: data simulated covariance relationship matrix. misspecified panel rejects, since data carry genetic effect independent across lines variance 6 genetic variance 10 relationship matrix. rejection says genetic covariance missing model, first stage correctly specified: first stage understates estimation error means also raises residual variance. extension paper examines adds effect model, identity kernel rotation WW′=Ω−1WW' = \Omega^{-1} . Without rotation effect residual error covariance matrix sum variances can estimated; two can separated, weakly Ω\Omega close proportional identity, dense design equal replication, panel unequal replication. deviance falls independent effect clearly present. free fit puts residual variance boundary zero, attributing estimation error independent effect; residual variance fixed known value one, independent effect estimated close generating value 6. paper adds effect model test rejects, evaluate scan extended model. package offers scan analysis can follow model test led ; residual variance zero model unweighted analysis adjusted means, scan says. components can instead held fit residual variance fixed known value one, fit = "residual_one"; residual scale still re-estimated marker, every scan.
code: std <- specification_test(rd) sts <- specification_test(rs) rm <- rotation(panel_misspecified$means, panel_misspecified$Omega, A, Q) stm <- specification_test(rm) sts #> Residual variance of the rotated model without a marker: 1.325 (target one; genetic variance 14.17, or 15.78 with the residual fixed at one) #> Increase in the REML deviance when the residual variance is fixed at one: 0.3487 #> One-sided test (residual above one): statistic 0.3487 against 2.71, not rejected (p = 0.277) #> Two-sided test: increase 0.3487 against 3.84, not rejected (p = 0.555) #> Profile-likelihood intervals for the residual variance: 90% [0.5319, 2.496], 95% [0.4206, 2.767] stm #> Residual variance of the rotated model without a marker: 3.192 (target one; genetic variance 21.91, or 32.52 with the residual fixed at one) #> Increase in the REML deviance when the residual variance is fixed at one: 4.335 #> One-sided test (residual above one): statistic 4.335 against 2.71, REJECTED: the residual variance is above one; genetic covariance is missing from the model, or the first stage understates the estimation error (see independent_effect()) (p = 0.0187) #> Two-sided test: increase 4.335 against 3.84, REJECTED: the residual variance differs from one (p = 0.0373) #> Profile-likelihood intervals for the residual variance: 90% [1.407, 5.485], 95% [1.112, 5.994] op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4, 3, 1)) plot(std, main = "dense panel") plot(stm, main = "misspecified panel") par(op) ## The model with the independent effect, against the additive model. ie <- independent_effect(rm) ie #> Rotated model with the relationship matrix and an effect independent across accessions (kernel WW') #> Genetic variance 16.6, independent effect 8.292, residual variance 0 (target one) [boundary: ve_zero] #>   The residual variance is at the boundary of zero: with it, this model is the unweighted analysis of the adjusted means. #> Against the additive model (genetic variance 21.91, residual 3.192): deviance lower by 5.963 (p = 0.0073 on the boundary mixture), AIC lower by 3.963 #> With the residual variance fixed at one: genetic variance 16.66, independent effect 6.407 #> Profile-likelihood intervals for the residual variance under this model: 90% [0, 2.11], 95% [0, 2.793] sm <- genome_scan(rm, G, model = ie) #> Warning in genome_scan(rm, G, model = ie): the residual variance of the model with the independent #> effect is at the boundary of zero; under it this scan is the unweighted analysis of the adjusted #> means summary(sm) #> Genome scan of 150 accessions, 4 fixed effects, 145 degrees of freedom per marker; Bonferroni threshold 4.602 in -log10 p at alpha 0.05; model: additive + independent effect #>   scheme genetic independent residual boundary inflation tested significant #>  rotated    16.6       8.292        0  ve_zero     0.888   1998           2 #>  #> Strongest markers, rotated: #>      marker  beta     se neglog10p #>  chr02_0185 2.577 0.5036     6.014 #>  chr02_0184 2.567 0.5165     5.730 #>  chr05_0017 2.019 0.4796     4.352 #>  chr05_0023 1.725 0.4142     4.273 #>  chr05_0018 1.907 0.5030     3.659 sm1 <- genome_scan(rm, G, model = ie, fit = "residual_one") summary(sm1) #> Genome scan of 150 accessions, 4 fixed effects, 145 degrees of freedom per marker; Bonferroni threshold 4.602 in -log10 p at alpha 0.05; model: additive + independent effect, residual variance fixed at one #>   scheme genetic independent residual boundary inflation tested significant #>  rotated   16.66       6.407        1     none     0.923   1998           2 #>  #> Strongest markers, rotated: #>      marker  beta     se neglog10p #>  chr02_0185 2.579 0.5034     6.025 #>  chr02_0184 2.557 0.5148     5.725 #>  chr05_0017 1.972 0.4794     4.186 #>  chr05_0023 1.702 0.4166     4.139 #>  chr05_0018 1.848 0.5050     3.453
